title: Personal Protective Equipment
whatItIs: PPE is equipment you wear or hold to protect you at work: hard hats, gloves, eye and hearing protection, hi-vis, safety boots and respirators. It is the last line of protection.

keyFacts.text: Employers MUST provide suitable PPE where a risk isn't adequately controlled by other means.
Employers MUST NOT charge workers for PPE the law requires them to provide.
Since 6 April 2022 employers MUST meet these PPE duties for casual 'limb (b)' workers as well as employees.
Workers MUST use PPE as trained and instructed, and return it to its storage after use.
Workers MUST report any loss of, or obvious defect in, their PPE to the employer at once.

keyFacts: PPE must fit the wearer and work with other PPE, e.g. ear defenders that fit onto a hard hat.

a.label: Employer's duties
points: Assess and provide suitable PPE, free

b.label: Worker's duties
points: Use it as trained and instructed
Return it to its storage after use
Report loss or defects at once

onTheTest.question: Your safety boots have split across the sole. What should you do?
options: Carry on until the job is finished
Report it to your employer straight away
onTheTest.why: PPE Regulations reg 11: every worker given PPE must report any loss or obvious defect to their employer straight away.

onTheTest.question: Who pays for PPE that a worker needs to do the job safely?
options: The worker, out of their wages
The employer: it must be free of charge
onTheTest.why: HSE: employers must provide PPE free of charge where it's needed. HSWA s9: no charge for anything the law requires.

traps: PPE is the last resort: removing or controlling the hazard comes first.
Casual 'limb (b)' workers get free PPE too, not only employees.
Dirty hi-vis doesn't do its job: badly soiled garments should be replaced.
A respirator won't seal over a beard: you need another type, e.g. an air-fed visor.
